name: PROMIS Scale v1.2 Global Health
developer: PROMIS Health Organization (Hays, Bjorner, Revicki, Spritzer and Cella, 2009)
construct: Global physical and mental health, including quality of life, physical function, pain, fatigue, emotional distress and social satisfaction.
licence: HealthMeasures (Northwestern University) has made English PROMIS measures available without charge for research and individual clinical use, with the copyright line retained. Since 2024 licence fees apply to translations and to vendor platforms such as Epic and the Assessment Center API. Confirm current terms on Steps to License. Form copyright line: "© 2010-2018 PROMIS Health Organization (PHO)".
instructions: Please respond to each question or statement by marking one box per row.

items.text: In general, would you say your health is:
items.note: Item code Global01. Response options: Excellent = 5, Very good = 4, Good = 3, Fair = 2, Poor = 1

items.text: In general, would you say your quality of life is:
items.note: Item code Global02. Response options: Excellent = 5, Very good = 4, Good = 3, Fair = 2, Poor = 1

items.text: In general, how would you rate your physical health?
items.note: Item code Global03. Response options: Excellent = 5, Very good = 4, Good = 3, Fair = 2, Poor = 1

items.text: In general, how would you rate your mental health, including your mood and your ability to think?
items.note: Item code Global04. Response options: Excellent = 5, Very good = 4, Good = 3, Fair = 2, Poor = 1

items.text: In general, how would you rate your satisfaction with your social activities and relationships?
items.note: Item code Global05. Response options: Excellent = 5, Very good = 4, Good = 3, Fair = 2, Poor = 1

items.text: In general, please rate how well you carry out your usual social activities and roles. (This includes activities at home, at work and in your community, and responsibilities as a parent, child, spouse, employee, friend, etc.)
items.note: Item code Global09r. Response options: Excellent = 5, Very good = 4, Good = 3, Fair = 2, Poor = 1

items.text: To what extent are you able to carry out your everyday physical activities such as walking, climbing stairs, carrying groceries, or moving a chair?
items.note: Item code Global06. Response options: Completely = 5, Mostly = 4, Moderately = 3, A little = 2, Not at all = 1

items.text: How often have you been bothered by emotional problems such as feeling anxious, depressed or irritable?
items.note: Item code Global10r. Response options: Stem: In the past 7 days... Never = 5, Rarely = 4, Sometimes = 3, Often = 2, Always = 1

items.text: How would you rate your fatigue on average?
items.note: Item code Global08r. Response options: Stem: In the past 7 days... None = 5, Mild = 4, Moderate = 3, Severe = 2, Very severe = 1

items.text: How would you rate your pain on average?
items.note: Item code Global07r. Response options: Stem: In the past 7 days... 0 (No pain) to 10 (Worst pain imaginable); recoded for scoring as 0 = 5, 1-3 = 4, 4-6 = 3, 7-9 = 2, 10 = 1

scoring: Each item is scored 1 to 5 with 5 the most favourable response (the 'r' coded items are printed with reversed values so that higher is always better; the 0 to 10 pain item is recoded 0 = 5, 1-3 = 4, 4-6 = 3, 7-9 = 2, 10 = 1). Sum the 4 Global Physical Health items (Global03, Global06, Global07r, Global08r) and the 4 Global Mental Health items (Global02, Global04, Global05, Global10r) for raw scores of 4 to 20 each, then convert each to a T score (mean 50, SD 10, US general population) with the HealthMeasures conversion tables. Global01 (general health) and Global09r (social roles) are scored individually and are not in either component. Higher T scores indicate better health. Component structure and pain recoding from the HealthMeasures PROMIS Global Health scoring manual (Hays et al., 2009), not from the form.
citation: Hays, R. D., Bjorner, J. B., Revicki, D. A., Spritzer, K. L., & Cella, D. (2009). Development of physical and mental health summary scores from the Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) global items. Quality of Life Research, 18(7), 873-880. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11136-009-9496-9
transcriptionNote: The HealthMeasures search page (itemsUrl) is a form driven search and returned no measure entries, so the items were transcribed from the RTI Cure Sickle Cell copy of the PROMIS Scale v1.2 Global Health form dated 13 April 2018 (sourceUrl). Item order and codes follow that form (Global01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 09r, 06, 10r, 08r, 07r). Items 6 and 7 were returned in fragments and joined with single spaces as the fetch instructed. The response scale differs by item; the default responseOptions is the Excellent to Poor set used by items 1 to 6, and each item's own options and any 'In the past 7 days...' stem are in its note. The form contains no scoring text; the component membership, recoding and T score method are from the HealthMeasures scoring manual and the Hays et al. (2009) article and should be checked against the current manual.
